title: Michael Caputo worked for Bloc Lytvyn in Ukraine in 2007
short_description: House testimony confirms Caputo briefly lived in Kyiv and worked on Bloc Lytvyn’s 2007 parliamentary campaign.
medium_description: Michael Caputo told the House Intelligence Committee on July 14, 2017, that he briefly lived in Kyiv in 2007 and worked on Bloc Lytvyn’s parliamentary campaign. The Kyiv Post separately reported his work for Volodymyr Lytvyn. Caputo later worked on Donald Trump’s presidential campaign. The evidence supports the year, rather than a specific relocation date.
long_description: Michael Caputo described his 2007 work in Ukraine during testimony to the House Intelligence Committee on July 14, 2017. He said he briefly lived in Kyiv and worked on the parliamentary election campaign of Bloc Lytvyn. A March 3, 2017, Kyiv Post account independently identified Caputo as an American political consultant who worked on Volodymyr Lytvyn’s 2007 campaign. The newspaper described Lytvyn as a former parliamentary speaker and former chief of staff to President Leonid Kuchma. In his testimony, Caputo explained that he worked for the party list, while also answering to its founder because the party was organized around his personality. Asked about the party’s alignment with Russia, Caputo said he did not recall whether it was considered pro-Russian. Caputo’s later Trump connection is documented in the same hearing: he described serving in the presidential campaign from approximately November 2015 to June 2016, initially directing its New York primary operation.

original_title: Eric Trump Foundation Fundraising Suspension Dated to December 2016
evidence_note: Contemporaneous NPR reporting dated December 22, 2016 verifies Eric’s withdrawal from direct fundraising; Nonprofit Quarterly separately dates the suspension announcement to December 22. Reuters documents the separate June 2017 inquiry. Proposed copy corrects chronology and does not allege the later inquiry caused suspension or establish diversion as adjudicated fact.
title: Eric Trump stops direct charity fundraising amid access concerns in December 2016
short_description: Eric Trump withdrew from direct fundraising for his foundation as donors’ possible access to the incoming president drew scrutiny.
medium_description: On December 22, 2016, contemporary reporting described Eric Trump’s decision to stop directly raising money for his charitable foundation. The move followed concerns that contributors might seek access to his father, President-elect Donald Trump. A separate New York attorney general inquiry reported in June 2017 concerned the charity’s payments and should not be treated as the cause of the earlier decision.
long_description: Eric Trump’s charitable fundraising drew scrutiny during the presidential transition because contributors could seek access to his father, President-elect Donald Trump. NPR reporting published on December 22, 2016, described Eric’s decision to stop directly soliciting donations for his foundation. The reporting placed the decision amid controversy over fundraising opportunities involving members of the Trump family, including an auction offering coffee with Ivanka Trump that had been canceled. Nonprofit Quarterly also reported a December 22 announcement suspending the foundation’s operations. The charity raised money for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital through activities including golf tournaments. The chronology is distinct from the New York attorney general’s examination of the foundation reported by Reuters in June 2017. That later inquiry concerned a report about money from charitable golf tournaments reaching Trump businesses. Reuters also noted Eric’s explanation that he had stopped direct fundraising at the end of 2016 to avoid the appearance of a conflict of interest.
